newsitem.title: GERMANY: Shippers greet end Lufthansa fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Shippers greet end Lufthansa fuel surcharge.

text.p: German air cargo shippers have welcomed the decision of Lufthansa Cargo AG to drop its cargo fuel surcharge.
The Federation of German Industry (BDI) transport department said there had been strong pressure on Lufthansa to drop the surcharge and it now expected other airlines to follow the move.
The Deutsche Lufthansa AG airfreight arm announced earlier it would drop its 10 US cents per kg fuel surcharge from April 15.
Fuel prices had now returned to the level of July 1996 and a renewed rise was not expected in the summer, the airline said in a statement.

A BDI transport department representative, who asked not to be named, told Reuters: "We welcome this move. Lufthansa Cargo has kept its promise to drop the surcharge when prices fell to July 1996 levels."
"There was pressure from the BDI on Lufthansa and as fuel prices fell we wanted Lufthansa to react. After Delta dropped the surcharge, Lufthansa was under pressure to do something," he stated.
In a letter to Lufthansa Cargo Germany director, Joachim Steinbach, in March, the BDI said fuel prices had fallen back to the levels of summer 1996 and the surcharge should be dropped immediately.
"Our members are urging that this step be taken," the letter said.
The BDI representative forecast: "All the others will now follow very quickly. They have no excuse not to."
The federation was not aware of any companies who had refused to pay the surcharge, he added.
